idiom_name: single-consumer async pipeline (promise chain or async iterator) plus a Map window
implementation_notes: JavaScript's event loop plus a single-consumer pipeline already preserves order, so the idiomatic answer is to keep the stream ordered by construction: await tasks one after another, chain promises, or pipe through a Readable/Transform stream, none of which needs a buffer. A classic resequencer is only needed when the disorder is real - several producers, worker_threads, or remote partitions - and then it is hand-written, because neither Node's standard library nor a dominant framework provides one: a Map keyed by sequence number (Map remembers insertion order) plus an expected-sequence cursor releases contiguous runs, and a single timer implements the gap policy.
pitfalls: Map preserves insertion order, not key order: scanning a Map for the smallest pending sequence number is wrong; drive delivery from the expected cursor instead.
A gap timer created per message both leaks timers and fires the policy for holes that were already closed; keep one timer per correlation and reset it on delivery.
Promise.all and worker_threads make completion order nondeterministic, so any post-processing that must be in order has to be sequenced by the cursor rather than by response arrival.
A CPU-bound gap handler blocks the event loop, postponing the very timeout that is supposed to unblock the stream.
